blocks.text: Between June 2026 and October 2026, detached houses: listings fell from 92 in June to 79 in October (−14.1%), and it took 9.7% of the city’s 464 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings fell from 147 in June to 123 in October (−16.3%), and it took 13.6% of the city’s 737 sales over the period.

The monthly write-ups singled out Sullivan Station for detached houses in October (a sellers’ best bet); detached houses in September (a buyers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in June, August (a sellers’ best bet).

blocks.text: Lots and land in Sullivan Station

items.t: Fee-simple detached lots — the land form that actually trades: A fee-simple lot carries no strata, no Form B and no strata fees; diligence is title, zone, SSMUH band and any riparian area on the parcel. South Newton lands carry R-series residential zones, with RA at the rural edges toward Colebrook, under Surrey Zoning Bylaw No. 12000.
Lot sizes: subdivision lots follow the Zoning Bylaw No. 12000 zone minimums for the lot's R-series zone.
Strata attached ground — cross-reference only, never re-counted

Assemblies / development sites: The documented development frame is plan-led: the rescinded South Newton plan no longer governs, designations were updated by Corporate Report R246 (endorsed December 2, 2024), and any site's potential is read off the Surrey 2050 OCP and Zoning Bylaw No. 12000, not off the old NCP.

Servicing: properties not connected to community water and sewer are among the exemptions from Surrey's SSMUH allowances — which is itself the servicing signal for a land buyer here: a lot's connection position changes what it can carry.
55+ position: No 55+ item is imported here as lot stock.

blocks.text: Where lots come up and what to know

items.t: Municipality and community: City of Surrey, in the Newton community. "Sullivan Station" is the SnapStats / board sub-area name for Surrey in the September 2026 report; the City does not publish a separate "Sullivan Station" plan boundary. The City's South Newton page describes South Newton as a large neighbourhood within the southeast of the broader Newton community, with neighbourhood commercial nodes including Panorama Heights at 152 Street and Hwy 10 and Sullivan Heights at 64 Ave and 144 Street — the Sullivan Station board sub-area sits inside that South Newton ground.

Plan ground: the South Newton plan area is approximately 485 hectares (1,200 acres), generally located north of Hwy 10, east of King George Boulevard and west of 152 Street, bordered by the East Newton NCPs to the northwest. Nearby areas: Panorama Ridge (south), East Newton (northwest), West Newton (west), Cloverdale (east, across the 152 Street side).

Plan status — read before relying on any older plan document: the South Newton plan was rescinded by the Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan update and is no longer in effect; development in this area is led by the Official Community Plan, and on December 2, 2024 Council endorsed Corporate Report R246, which updated land use designations to reflect current market conditions.
SD36 runs K–7 elementary and 8–12 secondary, with no middle-school tier.

Creeks: South Newton is home to several important fish-bearing creeks, including the headwaters of Archibald Creek, Sullivan Heights Creek and several tributaries of Hyland Creek — riparian/setback rules can therefore apply to creek-side lots in this area.

Transit: buses on the 152 St and 64 Ave corridors serve this area — route 321 runs via 152 St and King George Blvd, and route 322 runs via 132 St and 64 Ave between Newton and Scottsdale; the R1 RapidBus runs on King George Boulevard west of the area between Newton Exchange and King George Station via Surrey Central Station. No SkyTrain station is inside Sullivan Station.

The plan most sellers still name no longer exists. The South Newton plan was rescinded by the Surrey 2050 OCP update — a Sullivan Station lot marketed "per the South Newton NCP" is marketed off a dead plan, and the live frame is Surrey 2050 (Bylaw No. 21900) plus the R246 designation updates of December 2, 2024. This is the single most consequential land fact in the sub-area.
A new school redrew the catchment questions in January 2026.

The 280 m² line is a value line. Surrey's SSMUH bands step at 280 m² / 281 m² and again at frequent-bus-stop proximity — two near-identical teardown lots on the same Sullivan Station street can carry different unit counts, and the difference is measurable off the lot's surveyed area and the bus-stop map before an offer is written.

items.t: Sullivan Station has no separate City plan boundary of its own. The City ground here is South Newton, a large neighbourhood in southeast Newton with commercial nodes at Panorama Heights (152 Street and Highway 10) and Sullivan Heights (64 Avenue and 144 Street).
The South Newton plan area covers about 485 hectares, generally north of Highway 10, east of King George Boulevard and west of 152 Street, bordered by the East Newton plans to the northwest.
People say Sullivan Station, Sullivan or Sullivan Heights for this area, while the City names are Sullivan, Sullivan Heights and South Newton.

Housing here mixes detached houses with townhouse and low-rise infill around the two nodes. The City describes South Newton as having a variety of housing types, and a 2004 plan amendment added small-lot single-family designations.

A current infill shape is at 14188 62 Avenue, where a planning report proposes a 4-storey mixed-use building with 27 market rental homes and 513 square metres of ground-floor commercial space in South Newton.

blocks.text: Sullivan Station: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The South Newton plan no longer governs on its own. It was rescinded by the Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan (OCP) update, development is led by the OCP, and Council endorsed updated land-use designations on December 2, 2024 in Corporate Report R246.
Fish-bearing creeks cross this area, so creek lots need a setback check. South Newton holds the headwaters of Archibald Creek, Sullivan Heights Creek and tributaries of Hyland Creek.

blocks.text: Sullivan Station: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Catchments moved in January 2026, so last year's school answer may now be wrong. Snokomish Elementary opened that month for students from four existing school areas, which is why the locator, not the nearest school building, decides placement.

Six School District 36 schools sit in or serve this area: Sullivan Elementary (6016 152 Street), Cambridge Elementary (6115 150 Street), Goldstone Park Elementary (6287 146 Street), Woodward Hill Elementary (6082 142 Street), Snokomish Elementary (14778 58B Avenue) and Sullivan Heights Secondary (6248 144 Street).
Sullivan Heights Secondary holds about 1,550 students in Grades 8 to 12 and has the Bell Performing Arts Centre on site.
The 64 Avenue and 144 Street node is the walk-to node for the west side, while Panorama Heights at 152 Street and Highway 10 serves the east side — the two nodes split daily shopping for the area.
Creek headwaters run through the plan area, so a lot that looks like a normal rear yard can carry riparian limits on additions or a rebuild.

blocks.text: Sullivan Station: development and new projects

items.t: 14188 62 Avenue, South Newton — 4-storey mixed-use building, 27 market rental homes and 513 square metres of commercial space, with a housing agreement securing the homes as market rental for 40 years; status: planning report dated June 23, 2025 (as of November 3, 2026).
École Snokomish Elementary, 14778 58B Avenue — new 27-classroom Kindergarten to Grade 7 school; status: opened January 2026 (as of November 3, 2026).
Route 342 is the through route for this area. TransLink's timetable runs it from Newton Exchange via 72 Avenue, 144 Street, 60 Avenue, 152 Street and Highway 10 to Langley Centre.
Route 345 runs on 152 Street between King George Station and White Rock Centre via Fraser Highway and Highway 10, giving the east edge a direct link to SkyTrain at King George Station.

items.t: Check creek setbacks first on any lot touching Archibald Creek, Sullivan Heights Creek or a Hyland Creek tributary, using City mapping for the specific lot — the plan page names the creeks but does not set a lot's buildable area.

faq.q: Is there a bare-land subdivision or lot release in Sullivan Station?
faq.a: What trades as land is individual fee-simple detached lots under the R-series zones.

faq.q: What plan governs a Sullivan Station lot now?
faq.a: The Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 21900) and Zoning Bylaw No. 12000. The South Newton plan that covered this area was rescinded and is no longer in effect, and designations were updated by Corporate Report R246 (endorsed December 2, 2024). Never plan off Bylaw 18020 as a current OCP.

faq.q: How many units can a Sullivan Station house lot carry?
faq.a: Confirm the lot's band and bus-stop eligibility with the City before valuing a teardown or builder sale — and note an unpermitted existing suite is not legalized by the changes.

faq.q: Do creek rules really affect ordinary lots here?
faq.a: They can: Archibald Creek headwaters, Sullivan Heights Creek and Hyland Creek tributaries run through South Newton, and riparian/setback requirements can limit the building envelope on a creek-side lot. Check City mapping before valuing an addition or rebuild.

faq.q: Does GST apply when I buy a vacant lot here?
faq.a: It turns on the seller and the parcel's history, per CRA GI-003: an individual's personal-use sale is generally exempt, while a business sale or a parcel subdivided into more than two parts can be taxable, and a developer's newly subdivided lot is generally taxable. Have the contract state the position.

faq.q: Which secondary school serves Sullivan Station?
faq.a: Sullivan Heights Secondary at 6248 144 Street is the secondary school in this area.

faq.q: Can I add units to a detached lot here?
faq.a: Often yes, within the small-scale limits. Surrey allows up to 4 units on a lot over 280 square metres and up to 6 on an eligible lot near a frequent bus stop, and the City states these changes do not retroactively legalize a suite or coach house built without permits, so check permits on any existing suite.

No, there is no SkyTrain station in Sullivan Station. Service is by bus on the 152 Street and 64 Avenue corridors, with the R1 RapidBus on King George Boulevard west of the area linking Newton Exchange and King George Station, so a commute plan here starts with a bus leg.
